note: ADR-0006 template-owned path boundary. Ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix; a prefix ending in '/' matches a directory subtree, otherwise it matches an exact file. On a tie, user-owned wins (fail-closed: an upgrade never touches a path it isn't sure the template owns). Conservatively excludes apps/ (portal carries user/plugin pages) and infra/environments/ (per-instance config and secrets) for now; that boundary can widen later. services/api/migrations/versions/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned: Alembic migration files are an append-only, per-instance chain (each instance accumulates its own, chained by down_revision), so syncing them from the template breaks the instance's revision graph. It stays user-owned — the three-way merge must never rewrite an applied migration — but as of issue #198 `biffo core upgrade` runs a separate *additive* carry for it: new core migrations absent from the instance are appended, re-chained onto the instance's current head at upgrade time (and given a deterministic core_<hash> revision id if the template's own id is already taken in that instance), with the resulting chain validated for a single head before the PR is opened. Existing instance migrations are never modified, re-chained, or deleted. See cli/src/lib/core-migrations.ts. The migration framework itself (migrations/env.py, script.py.mako) stays template-owned. services/_plugins/ is template-owned even though services/ is user-owned: it is the carve-out that gives *first-party* plugins a distribution mechanism (issue #243). A plugin shipped in the template (e.g. orchestrator) previously sat directly under the user-owned services/, so `biffo core upgrade` fail-closed on it and the only channel left was manual PR copy-in — which is the absence of a mechanism, and let every instance's copy drift silently. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugins/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/api/ already does, so the underscore prefix (matching the existing services/_template/ convention, and un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name per registry-schema.json) is what declares ownership: a plugin under services/_plugins/ is the template's to maintain and is carried by every upgrade, while a third-party plugin installed into services/<name>/ stays the instance's and is never overwritten. Discovery (services/api/src/api/plugins.py) globs both locations, so the split is an ownership boundary only, never a runtime one. services/_plugin-host/ is template-owned for the same reason (ADR-0021): it is the shared plugin-host runtime the template maintains and every instance runs, so it needs a distribution channel or it drifts silently — the exact #243 failure. Without this carve-out `biffo core upgrade` fail-closes on it (services/ is user-owned), so the host Lambda provisioned by the template-owned infra/environments/dev/plugin-host.core.tf would ship but its code would never reach the instance, leaving it on the compute placeholder for ever. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugin-host/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/_plugins/ does; the underscore prefix (un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name) declares ownership. A plugin's own code stays under user-owned services/<name>/ and is mounted BY the host at deploy time (deploy-app.yml), never carried into the host source. services/pr-signer/ is template-owned for the same reason, and its own Terraform is split into infra/environments/dev/pr-signer.core.tf the same way plugin-host.core.tf carries the host's (issue #568). pr-signer is the isolated GitHub App credential holder for the endpoint control plane (ADR-0008) — platform/governance infrastructure every instance needs identically, not optional product code. It was left out of the original #243/#548 carve-out sweep: no code comment, ADR text, or manifest note anywhere ever stated a reason to exclude it, so this reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate choice, caught three weeks later by the same #243/#548 audit pattern run against it for the first time. Leaving it out meant a real post-launch fix — 0d97f5e ("fix(pr-signer): emit prettier-compatible JSON so permission PRs are minimal") — could ship in the template but never reach an already-scaffolded instance; only a manual PR copy-in could carry it, and nothing prompted anyone to do that. Unlike services/_plugins/ and services/_plugin-host/, the carved-out path is services/pr-signer/ without an underscore prefix: pr-signer is not a first-party member of the plugin system (it has no biffo.plugin.json, is not discovered by services/api/src/api/plugins.py, and is invoked over IAM directly rather than mounted by the plugin host), so it does not need the underscore convention's collision avoidance with a third-party plugin slug the same way those do. That leaves a narrow theoretical collision — a third-party plugin named exactly "pr-signer" — but the directory services/pr-signer/ already exists in every instance today regardless of this manifest entry, so `biffo plugin install` would already collide with it before this change; this carve-out changes who owns the bytes at that path, not whether the path is claimed. infra/environments/dev/pr-signer.core.tf is added to templateOwned alongside plugins.core.tf and plugin-host.core.tf for the same infra/environments/ carve-out reason (longest-prefix-wins over user-owned infra/); it carries the module "pr_signer" block, its Secrets Manager secret, and pr-signer's enable_pr_signer config-validation check block. It deliberately does NOT carry the invoke_function_arns argument or the BIFFO_PR_SIGNER_FUNCTION_NAME environment variable on module.core_api in main.tf — those stay on module.core_api's own block, which is not itself part of this carve-out, and they cross-reference module.pr_signer by name, which Terraform resolves regardless of which file in the directory declares the module. enable_pr_signer itself, and its pr_signer_github_app_id/pr_signer_github_installation_id/pr_signer_repo_owner/pr_signer_repo_name/pr_signer_base_branch companion variables, stay in the user-owned variables.tf: whether an instance runs the endpoint control plane at all, and which GitHub App/repo it targets, is legitimately per-instance policy, the same way enable_core_plugins stays user-owned policy layered on top of plugins.core.tf's template-owned wiring. apps/ is user-owned, but apps/portal/ within it is wholly template-owned (ADR-0006 longest-prefix wins). The portal is strictly the admin console (issue #306): it serves /admin and /login, the root path belongs to the user's application sibling, and nothing user-owned lives inside it. That portal code is a client of the Core API's admin surface — ~640 lines of *-api.ts calling /api/v1/admin/* — so it tracks the core API's version, not the instance's product. Leaving it user-owned meant template bugs in Biffo's own admin UI could not be distributed: #275 (navigation landing on the raw RSC payload) and #276 (login offering an unsupported identifier) both had to be hand-copied into every instance. #279 part 1 first tried this as a path-level carve-out (app/admin/, app/(auth)/, components/, lib/, context/), which was a trap: components/, lib/ and context/ are exactly where a user would put ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, and `core upgrade` would then propose deleting them. #306 removes the trap at its root by making the assumption explicit — the portal is not a canvas — rather than documenting around it, so the carve-out collapses to a single prefix. The instance's own product UI belongs in its application sibling repo, or in a NEW app under apps/, which stays user-owned by default. docs/ADR/ is user-owned: the template's ADRs are seeded once at `biffo init` as a starting point, but an instance's ADRs are its own decision record and legitimately diverge from the Biffo standard over time — force-syncing them on every core upgrade collides an instance's own ADR numbers with the template's and rewrites its history. Excluded from the sync flow for that reason; new template ADRs are announced in release notes rather than pushed into instances. The adr-numbering check (issue #1095, cli/src/lib/adr-numbering-guard.ts) that scans docs/ADR/ for numbering collisions does NOT violate the general rule stated below despite living in template-owned cli/: every function it exports takes the docs/ADR/ directory to scan as a parameter rather than resolving one of its own, and its only caller always passes the CURRENT repo's own docs/ADR/ (never a path belonging to a different repo) — so whichever repo it runs in owns everything it finds and can fix any real finding directly, with no upstream release required, the same shape already carved out for `*.instance.yml` in cli/src/lib/template-owned-scope.test.ts's allowedUnowned mechanism (issue #1096). Issue #1105 adds a second, narrower assertion to that same guard: in an INSTANCE repo only, a NEW docs/ADR/ file numbered inside adr-numbering-guard.ts's published TEMPLATE_ADR_RESERVED_UPTO boundary is flagged before it can ever collide with a template ADR not yet shipped, rather than only after, as the original collision check did. Both checks share one escape hatch, docs/ADR/.numbering-allowlist (added by #1097): a number an instance already legitimately holds — inherited at biffo init, or accepted as a permanent collision — is a one-time allowlist entry, not a blocked core upgrade. _skeletons/ is template-owned (issue #325). It is scaffolding *source* — the trees `biffo init` (step 6/6), `biffo sibling create` and `biffo plugin create` copy from — not instance content, and no instance ever reads its own copy: the CLI resolves a skeleton by walking UP from its own module (defaultSiblingTemplateRoot() in cli/src/commands/sibling-create.ts, findSkeletonRoot() in cli/src/lib/plugin-scaffold.ts), so an npm-installed CLI lands on the copy packaged beside its own dist/ (cli/scripts/packaged-root-assets.mjs, #315), never on the instance's. The instance has a copy only because `biffo init` clones the whole template repo, and it has been frozen at init time ever since. Leaving it unowned was the #325 trap: cli/ IS template-owned, so the non-interactive-Terraform guard added in #322 (cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.ts) was distributed to every instance while the skeleton workflows it scans were not — every upgrade to 0.41.3 landed a guard whose subject the upgrade had no mechanism to fix, and instance CI went red on files the instance neither wrote nor could repair (reproduced on keiranholloway/biffo-platform PR #1). The general rule: a template-owned check must never assert over paths the template does not own. Same argument as services/_plugins/ (#243) — a path the template maintains needs a distribution channel, or it drifts silently in every instance, which is how the #322 bug survived unnoticed in the first place. This is NOT a repeat of the #279 part-1 trap: components/, lib/ and context/ were a trap because they are exactly where a user would put their own ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, whereas there is nowhere inside _skeletons/ a user would legitimately add a file. Customising the scaffold is done by pointing `biffo sibling create --template <path>` at your own tree — an explicitly supported flag — not by editing the inherited copy. Making it owned also re-syncs the template-owned tests that read it (cli/src/lib/secret-scan-scope.test.ts, cli/src/adapters/source-control/github/status-checks.test.ts) with their subject, and cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.test.ts now asserts every path the guard scans resolves as template-owned, so the mismatch cannot silently return. There is no core.version file to own since issue #423: the version the *template emits* is derived from its core-v* tags, so nothing in the tree names it and there is nothing to sync. The version an instance *received* is recorded in the userOwned biffo.core.json, which is what every lookup reads (cli/src/lib/core-version.ts). Issue #327 (audit follow-up to #325) swept the remaining template-owned checks that asserted over unowned paths and scoped each to template-owned code: the plugin-terraform guard (cli/src/lib/plugin-terraform-guard.ts) now filters discovered manifests through isTemplateOwned so a third-party plugin under user-owned services/<name>/ never reds a template-shipped gate; the CI infra-validate job fmt-checks and terraform-validates only modules/ (never user-owned infra/environments/, whose hardcoded dev env an instance may rename or remove); bandit runs over services/api and services/_plugins only (not the instance's own services/); ruff excludes _skeletons (matching pyright) and db/; and .prettierignore (now template-owned, so the scoping distributes) excludes the user-owned trees the format gate used to reach (apps/ except apps/portal, services/ except the template-owned services, infra/, docs/, README.md, biffo.* config). The general rule is encoded as an executable META guard in cli/src/lib/template-owned-scope.test.ts, with a negative control so it cannot pass by matching its own prose. pnpm-workspace.yaml's apps/* glob is left as-is: enrolling a new user app into the monorepo's shared lint/type/test is the point of a monorepo and the user opts in by creating the app there (the gate fires only on the user's own code, which the user can fix — not the #325 class where the subject is un-fixable inherited content). core-migrations.test.ts's real-tree single-head assertion is now skipped when biffo.core.json is present (i.e. in an instance), so it validates only the template's own shipped chain, never the instance's user-owned migrations/versions/. .githooks/commit-msg, .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are template-owned as EXACT FILES, not the .githooks/ directory (issue #370, moved there by #838). The hooks moved out of .husky/ because husky's runner directory .husky/_ is gitignored and generated only by `prepare` on `pnpm install`, while core.hooksPath is a RELATIVE path git resolves per worktree -- so every fresh worktree had no .husky/_ and git skipped every hook silently. Verified on tabsii-platform/.worktrees/discovery-rls, which carried the three tracked hook files, no .husky/_, and therefore no pyright, no lint-staged and no commitlint on any commit made there. A tracked hooks directory is present the instant a worktree exists, with no install step. The .husky/ files remain as forwarders for clones that have not re-run install since the upgrade and whose core.hooksPath still points at .husky/_; deleting them would disarm those clones silently, which is the failure being fixed. Same EXACT FILE reasoning as before: The template wires the hooks it ships -- commitlint, lint-staged, and the core-ownership guard -- and those wirings must reach instances or the guard exists only in the repo that does not need it. Owning the whole directory would be the #279 part-1 trap in another costume: an instance's own pre-push or post-merge hook is exactly the sort of file a user legitimately adds, and a template-owned subtree would propose deleting it. Exact-file entries own the two hooks the template actually writes and leave the rest of .husky/ to the instance. biffo.divergence.json is user-owned by the same reasoning as the other biffo.*.json files: it records which template-owned prefixes THIS instance knowingly diverges in (warn instead of block), which is per-instance policy the template must never overwrite -- and if it were template-owned, the guard would block the commit that configures the guard. infra/environments/dev/plugins.core.tf is template-owned even though infra/ is user-owned (longest-prefix-wins, same carve-out shape as apps/portal/ inside apps/): it provisions the first-party agentic plugins (orchestrator, agent-runtime) as core capability (ADR-0014), closing #406. The instantiation used to be hand-wired per instance in the user-owned main.tf and drifted — tabsii had it, a fresh instance had nothing and its agents were dead. Making just this file template-owned distributes the wiring and keeps every instance in parity, while leaving the rest of infra/environments/ (per-instance account/domain/secret config) user-owned. It depends only on the template-seeded shape every instance has (var.project_name, local.environment, local.tags, module.events, module.api_gateway) and passes the OpenRouter credential by SSM-path convention rather than a per-instance variable, so it upgrades cleanly into an older instance whose variables.tf never gained the plugin vars. The plugin-allowlist module's core_plugins default lists the same first-party set so those Lambdas reach /api/v1/internal/* with no edit to the user-owned root config; the two lists are kept in step (adding a first-party plugin touches both). .gitleaks.toml is template-owned as an exact file (#516), same reasoning as the .husky hooks (#370): the template ships the Secret Scan rules AND the code those rules must not flag, so it must be able to ship the allowlist that keeps them consistent — otherwise a template-shipped literal (e.g. the fck-nat vendor AMI-owner id, #514) reds every instance's Secret Scan on content the instance didn't write and can't diagnose (which is exactly what happened when the fck-nat module reached tabsii and biffo-platform). biffo core upgrade three-way-merges it, so a template rule/allowlist change distributes while an instance-added allowlist entry (a distinct line in the regexes/paths arrays) survives the merge; only a same-line edit conflicts. This is not the #279-part-1 trap: instance additions are preserved by the merge rather than proposed for deletion, and there is no place inside a shared scanner ruleset a user adds product code — product-specific allowlisting is an additive entry, not a competing file. modules/plugins/ is user-owned even though modules/ is template-owned (longest-prefix-wins), because `biffo plugin install` copies a THIRD-party plugin's terraform/ into modules/plugins/<name>/ (ADR-0003) — that copy is instance content the template will never ship, so an ownership guard marking it template-owned blocks the very install that writes it, and a core upgrade would propose deleting it. Same shape as a third-party plugin under user-owned services/<name>/. modules/plugins/_template/ is carved back to template-owned (a longer prefix still wins): it is the scaffold source `biffo plugin create` copies from, maintained by the template like _skeletons/, and rides core upgrade. First-party plugins are unaffected — their terraform lives in template-owned services/_plugins/<name>/ and is referenced in place (never copied into modules/plugins/). CI still terraform-validates modules/ (so a third-party plugin module is validated), and core upgrade simply never carries modules/plugins/<name>/. AGENTS.md is template-owned as an EXACT FILE (issue #559), same reasoning as CLAUDE.md (#370-class): it is the tool-agnostic rules of engagement CLAUDE.md imports (@AGENTS.md) and the single source of truth for agent/dev practice in every repo, so it must reach instances or it drifts silently -- which is exactly what happened and is what #559 is: tabsii's copy fell 68 lines behind the template's, missing the very workflow guardrails (masked-push detection, reproduce-the-bug-first, fresh-worktree-with-deps-sync discipline) the template had already written, because AGENTS.md was in neither ownership list and fail-closed to user-owned. Making it a templateOwned exact file (not the repo root, which stays user-owned) distributes it via biffo core upgrade like CLAUDE.md; the three-way merge preserves any genuine instance-specific addition while carrying template rule changes, and since the instances hold no such additions today (both were pure stale subsets of the template's) the first upgrade simply brings them current. Plugin and sibling repos are separate repos core upgrade never reaches, so they get AGENTS.md by vendoring it into _skeletons/plugin-template/ and _skeletons/sibling-template/ (every newly scaffolded repo) plus a one-time manual copy-in for existing ones -- the same distribution split every user-owned-repo artifact uses. CONTRIBUTING.md is template-owned for the same reason: it is a three-line pointer at AGENTS.md (no instance-specific content), so distributing it keeps every repo's contribution entry-point consistent rather than template-only. services/api/src/api/domains/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned (longest-prefix-wins, ADR-0022, issue #547): it is an instance's home for its OWN product-domain code (models, routers, events, schemas, tests) INSIDE the core API. ADR-0002 makes the core the single data plane -- the platform owns the data and applications are guests -- so a product's canonical relational domain belongs in the core DB/API by design (a sibling holds no DB per ADR-0007; a plugin owns no data per ADR-0003). But everything else under services/api/ is template-owned, so before this carve-out an instance could not edit its own domain code without the core-ownership guard blocking the commit and biffo core upgrade treating it as template drift (the exact snag that surfaced this: tabsii's tabsii.* schema and ~15 routers). This is the same shape as services/api/migrations/versions/ (user-owned inside template-owned services/api/): a longest-prefix-wins carve-out for legitimately-per-instance content. Discovery stays template-owned and distributes -- api.routing.domain_router globs domains/<name>/ and mounts each domain's exported routers, so main.py (template-owned) never needs a per-instance edit -- while the domains themselves are the instance's to maintain and are never carried by an upgrade. db/imports/<name>/ (DDL-imported schemas) is already covered: db/ is user-owned. The domains/ tree is seeded once (an __init__.py + README) like docs/ADR/, then owned by the instance; the base template ships no product domain, so build_domain_router mounts nothing there. services/api/tests/instance/ and modules/**/instance/ are user-owned (issue #1026): a sanctioned home for tests an INSTANCE writes under an otherwise template-owned tree. Before this carve-out such a file had nowhere sanctioned to live, so it resolved template-owned and only ever showed up on `biffo core upgrade`'s orphan report (the `!inBase && !inTheirs` branch of classify() in cli/src/lib/core-upgrade.ts, status `keep-ours`) as unsanctioned drift -- a warning that can never go clean on a single instance is one people learn to ignore. scripts/verify-deployed.checks is user-owned too (issue #1706), a single exact-file carve-out rather than a subtree one: its own header already claimed "INSTANCE-OWNED ... seeded, never overwritten by a sync", but that claim was a comment enforced nowhere, and scripts/ is template-owned as a bare prefix with no override, so the file resolved TEMPLATE -- the opposite of what it promised. The failure mode is not the safe orphan case above: this file is a real path the template ALSO ships (as a comment-only stub), so an instance that seeds it with real checks and a template that later ships the same path hit classify()'s `!inBase && inTheirs && inOurs` add-conflict branch, which resolves to the template's bytes verbatim -- the instance's real checks silently overwritten by the stub on the next `biffo core upgrade`, flagged conflicted but not blocked. Carving the one file out means it never reaches classify() as template-owned at all, the same mechanism #1026 uses, so the clobber is unrepresentable rather than merely detected. modules/**/instance/ needed a `**` segment rather than a single `*`: modules/ nests provider/module subtrees to an unpredictable depth (modules/cloud/aws/networking/instance/, modules/source-control/github/instance/, and so on), and a single-segment `*` can only name a carve-out at one fixed depth. globToRegExp (cli/src/lib/core-manifest.ts) now treats a `**` path segment as zero-or-more whole segments, crossing `/` -- the one deliberate exception to the narrower-than-a-shell-glob rule `*` has followed since #755, added for exactly this case and no other; a lone `*` elsewhere in the same pattern is still segment-local. The orphan report itself is a ratchet, not a hard block: it reuses this SAME isTemplateOwned resolution (deliberately not a second notion of ownership) to find template-owned paths present only in the instance, excludes gitignored/untracked ones (a build artifact is not a classification target, same reasoning as #1006), and records the count on first sight in the instance-owned biffo.orphan-baseline.json -- also added to userOwned here, for the same reason biffo.divergence.json is: the file that records an instance's own state must never itself be blocked from being written by the guard it feeds. An upgrade fails only when a LATER count exceeds that recorded baseline; it never hard-fails on the pre-existing residue. apps/portal/src/instance-<name>.ts and its .test.ts sibling are user-owned inside template-owned apps/portal/ (longest-prefix-wins), one pair per ADR-0028 seam declared in apps/portal/next.config.ts's instanceSeams. The seam file is the instance's declaration; the test is how the instance asserts what its own declaration resolves to, and it is NOT optional decoration. A seam's values are instance data, so no template test can ever cover them: login-routing.test.ts deliberately INJECTS six distinct destinations to test rule precedence, and must, because against the real map five of six outcomes are /admin/ and those assertions would go quiet rather than red. Carving out the declaration and not its test therefore leaves the values untestable ANYWHERE, which is #1307 -- and #1306 did exactly that, having fixed the mirror-image half (#1305: the seam resolved via next.config.ts's alias and the guard refused any instance that authored it, so every instance served the generic default and every non-admin tabsii user was routed to /admin/ and refused by AuthGuard). Both halves are one mechanism: a seam must be resolvable, authorable AND testable, and each half looks complete on its own because it lives in a different file. cli/src/lib/portal-seam-carveout.test.ts derives both required paths FROM instanceSeams rather than listing them, so adding a third seam cannot forget either. The template defaults these resolve to (apps/portal/src/lib/instance-nav-empty.ts, apps/portal/src/lib/login-destinations-default.ts) stay template-owned and are asserted so: carving one out would let an instance edit the fallback every other instance shares. infra/environments/dev/plugin-storage.core.tf is template-owned for the same infra/environments/ carve-out reason as plugins.core.tf, plugin-host.core.tf and pr-signer.core.tf (longest-prefix-wins over user-owned infra/): it grants the Core API's execution role the S3 PutObject/GetObject permissions that back the plugin object-storage capability (ADR-0021, #1437) -- the presigned-URL upload/download endpoints in api.plugin_storage. #1448 ("feat(storage): give plugins object storage the host provisions") added the file itself -- whose own header comment already declares it "TEMPLATE-OWNED (ADR-0021, biffo-template#1437)" -- and its guard test, services/api/tests/test_plugin_storage_prefix_grant.py, but never added the path to this manifest, so `biffo core upgrade` fail-closed on it exactly like #325/#327 (a template-owned check asserting over a path the template does not distribute): the guard's own "guard the guard" assertion, test_the_terraform_file_is_where_this_test_thinks_it_is, failed on every instance the moment it upgraded to core 0.272.0, because the file the guard checks for genuinely never arrived (biffo-template#1452, surfaced by tabsii-platform's 0.264.0 -> 0.272.0 upgrade, tabsii-com/tabsii-platform#849). It depends only on the template-seeded shape every instance has -- module.storage.plugin_media_bucket_arn and module.core_api.role_name, both unconditional blocks in main.tf since the storage and core-api modules were introduced -- so it upgrades cleanly into any instance regardless of age, the same dependency shape plugins.core.tf documents for itself. infra/environments/dev/core-api-environment.core.tf is template-owned for the same infra/environments/ carve-out reason as the four .core.tf files above (longest-prefix-wins over user-owned infra/). It exists because `module "core_api"` is declared in the USER-OWNED infra/environments/dev/main.tf with `environment_variables` as a literal map inside that block, and Terraform has no mechanism for a second file to add an argument to a module block another file declares -- arguments are not additive across files, and _override.tf replaces an argument rather than merging into it. So no template-owned file could ever carry a new environment variable into an instance's Core API; not "was not carrying one", could not. Two live casualties: BIFFO_PLUGIN_MEDIA_BUCKET (#1538), where plugin-storage.core.tf distributes the IAM grant but the bucket NAME existed only on a hand-written line in the template's own main.tf -- confirmed absent from the live tabsii-platform-dev-core-api Lambda, so api.plugin_storage._bucket() raises and plugin object storage has never worked in any instance; and BIFFO_PR_SIGNER_FUNCTION_NAME (#1540), same file, same block, whose non-distribution pr-signer.core.tf's own header had already described accurately and left in place. The fix is the mechanism module "plugin_host" already has (#1534): the module block consumes a merge() whose first argument is declared in a template-owned file, so the template gains somewhere to put a key that is not the module block itself. It declares BOTH `variable "core_api_environment"` (per-instance extra config, the counterpart to plugin_host_environment) AND `local.core_api_environment` = merge(var.core_api_environment, { the two core keys }), and main.tf's adoption is the single line `environment_variables = merge(local.core_api_environment, {`. The local is needed where plugin-host.core.tf uses a bare var because a root-module variable's default may only be a constant expression -- it cannot reference module.storage or module.pr_signer, which is exactly what both casualties are -- and plugin_host does not hit that because ITS literal map is itself in a template-owned file. Precedence matches the precedent exactly: the caller-supplied map is merged FIRST and the template's core keys SECOND, so a core key can never be silently overridden by instance config. It depends only on the template-seeded shape every instance has (module.storage.plugin_media_bucket_name, module.pr_signer/var.enable_pr_signer -- the same references main.tf and pr-signer.core.tf already make), so it upgrades cleanly into any instance. IMPORTANT: distributing this file changes nothing on its own. Until an instance applies that one line to its own user-owned main.tf, the variable and local exist and are simply unread -- the same one-time adoption module "plugin_host" never needed because it was born template-owned. This closes the environment-variable case only; a future template change needing a non-env-var module ARGUMENT on module.core_api still has no channel, and fixing that class means moving module "core_api" wholesale into a .core.tf file (option 2 in #1538), left as a separate decision. infra/global/main.tf is template-owned as a narrow exact-file carve-out inside the broader user-owned infra/ (issue #1584, owner decision B recorded on #1584 2026-08-23T07:02:19Z): it holds the error_status_demote Lambda@Edge (aws_iam_role.error_status_demote, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.error_status_demote_logs, aws_lambda_function.error_status_demote) that pairs with modules/cloud/aws/cdn/variables.tf's template-owned error_status_restore_lambda_arn plumbing -- the half of that mechanism that actually creates the Lambda previously sat on the user-owned side of the boundary from the module that consumes its ARN, so a template fix to the demote Lambda had no distribution channel into an already-scaffolded instance and could only be hand-copied. The carve-out is deliberately scoped to main.tf alone, not the whole infra/global/ directory: infra/global/outputs.tf (which produces the ARN via aws_lambda_function.error_status_demote.qualified_arn) and infra/global/variables.tf carry the rest of that same plumbing and were not surveyed for cross-instance divergence before this change went in, so widening the carve-out to them is deliberately left undone rather than assumed safe -- do not fold them in without repeating the same instance-by-instance divergence check this entry's history records.
